prerequisites: Having acquired the competencies of previous educational stages. It is recommended to have studied Chemistry in Baccalaureate.

learning_outcomes.text: Ability to understand and apply the principles of basic knowledge of general chemistry, organic and inorganic chemistry and their applications in engineering.
Knowledge in basic and technological subjects, which enables them to learn new methods and theories, and provides them with versatility to adapt to new situations.
Ability to solve problems with initiative, decision-making, creativity, critical reasoning, and to communicate and transmit knowledge, skills and abilities in the field of Industrial Engineering.

Democratic values and sustainability. Develop commitment to the society we live in so that it prospers through the dimensions of democratic values and sustainability, materialized within the global framework that defines it at all times.
Handles the basic principles of general chemistry, organic chemistry and inorganic chemistry.
Handles the basic laws that regulate reactions: thermodynamics, kinetics and equilibrium.
Solves exercises and problems completely and logically.
Applies theoretical concepts appropriately in the laboratory by correctly and safely using basic material and equipment.
Presents and interprets data and results.

syllabus_topics: The atoms: atomic model and electronic structure.
Kinetic and thermodynamic aspects of chemical reactions.
Chemical bonding: ionic, covalent, and metallic.
States of matter and phase changes.
Main group elements: metals and non-metals.
Critical and systemic vision of democratic society, promoting respect and equality among all people.
Main current challenges of the planet: identification, importance, and relationship with the SDGs of the 2030 Agenda.
assessment_rules: For continuous assessment, the final grade is calculated as 0.5*P1 + 0.4*P2 + 0.1*L. A minimum grade of 4 is required in each part (P1, P2, L) to average. In the global evaluation, students can retake pending parts or seek to improve their grade; the same formula and minimums apply, and a practical lab exam is required if laboratory practices were not done. For the extraordinary call, a global written exam covers all theoretical and practical concepts, and previous grades are not considered; a practical lab exam is required if laboratory practices were not done. Authorship of evaluated work must be demonstrable, otherwise the activity's grade will be zero.
